## When and where

This message is for Alabama for the 48-hour period from 7 p.m. CDT Thursday, October 8, to 7 p.m. CDT Saturday, October 10. National Weather Service Flood Watches cover the whole state — all 67 counties.

## Flood risk

Flood risk is highest in south Alabama, especially Escambia, Baldwin, Conecuh, Monroe, Geneva, Clarke, Covington, Mobile, Houston, Washington, and Wilcox counties. Forecast river flooding includes moderate flooding on Bayou Sara at Saraland and the Styx River near Elsanor.

## Expected rainfall

South Alabama: 4 to 8 inches, with local amounts up to 15 inches possible.  
Central Alabama: 2 to 4 inches, with local amounts up to 5 inches.  
North Alabama: 2 to 4 inches, with local amounts up to 7 inches.

## Uncertainty

The main uncertainty is where the heaviest rain bands will set up. A small shift could move the greatest flooding threat from one county to another. Some areas may get much less rain, while nearby communities could see much higher totals.

## What to do

Never drive through flooded roads. The National Weather Service message is: Turn Around, Don’t Drown. Know your route to higher ground, or have a plan and supplies ready if you need to stay in place. Monitor the National Weather Service and your county emergency management agency. Follow evacuation orders from local officials. Mobile and Baldwin County residents should also follow the hurricane and storm surge warnings.

## Sources and updates

Sources include NHC Advisory 9A, issued 6:51 p.m. CDT October 8; National Weather Service Flood Watches; and WPC outlooks issued October 8 at 15:59Z, 20:31Z, and 20:15Z. Check again with official sources at the next NHC advisory, expected at 10 p.m. CDT.
